newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - November 26.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
President Chandrika Kumaratunga, who arrived in Paris on Sunday for an official visit, meets with French President Jacques Chirac at Elysee Palace.

A special burn unit set up at Sri Lanka's foremost hospital for children, Lady Ridgeway Hospital. About seven percent of deaths in the island are caused by burn injuries. Most victimes are children, health officials say.
A separatist Tamil Tiger suicide bomber attacks vehicle of senior police officer in the east, killing himself and critically wounding the driver. The official was not in the vehicle at the time.
Nine Sri Lankan Tamils presumed dead in the Ethiopian airline crash.

Singapore Airlines plane with 133 passengers on board ordered to return to Colombo airport shortly after takeoff after being informed of a possible bomb abord. Authorities searched the aircraft, but found nothing.

Opportunities for Sri Lankans to work in South Korea gradually diminish as nearly half of all Sri Lankans employeed there have ignored their contracts and worked for other organisations, Foreign Employment Bureau says.
Bank employees protest planned privatisation of State Mortgage and Investment Bank. Say they will oppose moves to privatise any state bank.
President Kumaratunga meets with French President Jacques Chirac at Elysee Palace for bilateral talks.

International Red Cross officials say Tamil rebels claim they have not captured any soldiers alive during their successful attack on the northeastern Mullaitivu army camp. In July, the rebels overran the camp which was manned by more than 1,200 troops.
Tamil rebels ask people in four villages near the eastern Valachchenai army camp to evacuate. Security forces say they are prepared to face a major attack on the camp by rebels.
